verses.english: The devas attending on the sun came, with the sun before them.
Putting the constellations before them, the Mandabalāhakas came.
Vāsava, chief of the Vasus, Sakka the Purindada, came too.
These ten, tenfold hosts, all of varied hues,
possessed of power, of radiance, of beauty and of renown,
came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.
Then came the Sahabhū devas, blazing like the crest of a fire,
the Ariṭṭhakas and the Rojas, shining like flax flowers.

verses.pali_roman: Varuṇā sahadhammā ca accutā ca anejakā.
verses.english: The Varuṇas and the Sahadhammas, the Accutas and the Anejakas.
The Sūleyyas and Rucirās came. The Vāsavanesis came.
These ten, tenfold hosts, all of varied hues,
possessed of power, of radiance, of beauty and of renown,
came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.
The Samānas and Mahāsamānas, the Mānusas and Mānusuttamas.
The Khiḍḍāpadūsikas came. The Manopadūsikas came.

verses.pali_roman: Athāgū harayo devā ye ca lohitavāsino.
verses.english: Then came the Harī devas, and those clothed in red.
The Pāragas and Mahāpāragas came, devas of renown.
These ten, tenfold hosts, all of varied hues,
possessed of power, of radiance, of beauty and of renown,
came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.

verses.pali_roman: Sukkā karumhā aruṇā āgū veghanasā saha.
verses.english: The Sukkas, Karumhas and Aruṇas came, with the Veghanasas.
The Odātagayhas and the foremost ones came, discerning devas.
The Sadāmattas, Hāragajas and Missakas, of renown.

verses.pali_roman: Thanayaṃ āgā pajunno, yo disā abhivassati.
verses.english: Pajjunna came thundering, who rains upon the quarters.
These ten, tenfold hosts, all of varied hues,
possessed of power, of radiance, of beauty and of renown,
came rejoicing to the wood, to the assembly of bhikkhus.

vocabulary.meaning: the lunar mansions or constellations, put before the cloud-devas in the procession
devas ruined by play and devas ruined by mind — two classes whose names describe how they fall from their state
the rain-god, who comes thundering and rains upon the quarters
the flax flower, pale blue. The Aritthakas and Rojas are said to shine like it
